thread.title: Investigate Unresolved Links
thread.preview:
**I acquired additional FBI, FDLE and court records, but no original Prestancia visitor log, license-plate image, or completed gate-plate comparison.** The acquired records document several actual transfers and a residence-vehicle investigation. They do **not authenticate the reported Atta/Jarrah gate match or establish a Sarasota connection to UMS or Max**.

Below, page numbers are **one-based PDF pages**, with internal/Bates numbers where available. “Acquired” means I downloaded and inspected the public copy; it does not mean possession or forensic authentication of the physical original.

## 1. Acquired records and custody

The most useful addition to the supplied chronology is the **November 27, 2017** production in *Broward Bulldog v. DOJ*, **0:12-cv-61735-WJZ**: **DE 97-2, “Updated Universe of Documents Released to Plaintiffs (Redacted)”**, 79 pages, and **DE 97-3, “Index Explaining the Location of Responsive Records (Redacted)”**, 11 pages. I acquired both the index and the underlying pages discussed below. The index alone would establish only a file-location reference. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

| Record | Exact location | What the acquired record establishes |
|---|---|---|
| **Gate operations and management** | Larry Berberich declaration, **January 20, 2013**, DE 29-2, reproduced in **DE 99-1, pp. 117–119**, especially ¶¶4–5; Jone Barlow Weist declaration, **January 12, 2013**, DE 29-3, reproduced at **pp. 121–124** | Berberich describes responsibility for two gates and recording visitors’ and host residents’ names. Weist identifies Barlow Group’s management role during **2000–2008**, followed by Gulfside Islands Corporation. Neither declaration supplies a gate-log transfer or retention schedule. |
| **Actual HOA document transmission** | Barlow Group fax, **September 20, 2001**, **DE 97-2, pp. 38–41 / BULLDOG-40–43** | A transmittal and accompanying payment documents concerning 4224 Escondito Circle. **DE 97-3, p. 7** identifies the FBI recipient and location: **265A-NY-280350-TP, section 73, pp. 102–105**. |
| **Actual FBI evidence envelope** | **FD-340**, received **July 23, 2002**, **DE 97-2, p. 37 / BULLDOG-39** | Tampa evidence envelope titled **“ESAM GHAZZAWI”**; originating serial **2**, evidence section **1A, serial 1**. Its described contents are a copied letter and telephone-number list. “Receipt Given” is marked **No**. |
| **Sheriff/FDLE information transfers** | **FDLE FM-48-0040, IR 253**, activity date **April 28, 2004**, **DE 100-2, pp. 1–2**; **SI-73-1999, IR 1**, **pp. 10–12** | A retrospective account of Berberich supplying information to Lt. John Kost on **November 1, 2001**, and contact information being forwarded on **November 9**. The separate financial-background report states that its information was provided to Kost on **September 17, 2002**. These are information transfers, not documented gate-media transfers. |

The declarations are reproduced in [DE 99-1, Declaration of Thomas R. Julin and attachments](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/DE-099-1-Declaration-of-Thomas-R.-Julin.pdf). The government records are in [DE 97-2](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/DE-97-2-Universe-of-Documents.pdf), its [location index](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/DE-097-3-Index-Explaining-Location-of-Responsive-Records.pdf), and the [FDLE exhibit](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2018/07/DE-100-2-FDLE-Memo-re-Interview-of-WIssam-Taysir-Hammoud-re-Abdulaziz-al-Hijji.pdf). :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

Two custody qualifications matter:

- Weist recalled supplying check copies by approximately **April 2002**; the acquired fax establishes an earlier transmission on **September 20, 2001**. These could concern separate productions or an imprecise recollection.
- Berberich’s declaration describes sheriff personnel removing a **telephone and answering machine**—**DE 99-1, p. 119, ¶9**. It does not establish removal of gate logs, photographs or recording equipment. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"}

**Retention remains unknown.** I located no gate-system vendor record, recording format, coverage inventory, retention/overwrite policy, destruction certificate or successor-custodian acknowledgment. The **30-day period** in the postal interview concerns **undelivered mail**, not gate images: supplied *Government Exhibits*, **p. 48 / SARASOTA-18**. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"}

## 2. TP2844 is a residence-vehicle lead

The supplied [Government Exhibits](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2012/09/Government-Exhibits.pdf), **DE 25-2, filed May 13, 2013**, contain:

- **P. 45 / SARASOTA-15:** FD-822 dated **September 20, 2001**, recording information received **September 19 at 12:25 p.m.**, control **TP2844**. A postal inspector reported a Chevrolet Tahoe; its plate is redacted.
- **P. 48 / SARASOTA-18:** postal interview, transcribed **September 25**, describing a vehicle in the driveway.
- **Pp. 53–55 / SARASOTA-23–25:** **September 25, 2001** FBI communication; **p. 54** describes a **1995 four-door Chevrolet** registered to a redacted person at the residence. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}

I also acquired the handwritten lead copies. **DE 97-2, p. 53 / BULLDOG-55** marks TP2844 covered on **September 25, 2001**, recording an interview report and communication passed to the counterterrorism unit. The index identifies **265D-NY-280350-TP, serial 2641**, with this copy in **265A-NY-280350-TP, section 73, p. 106**. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="5"}

**That is a documented disposition of the postal/residence lead.** It is not a disposition of an Atta/Jarrah visitor-gate comparison. The redactions prevent matching its plate, VIN or registered person to another vehicle record.

## 3. The Atta/Jarrah claim and counterevidence

### The positive claim

The earliest located public account is Summers and Christensen’s **September 8, 2011** article. It attributes to Berberich and an unnamed counterterrorism officer the claim that photographed plates and visitor-name information matched **Atta and Jarrah** visiting **4224 Escondito Circle**. It publishes **no plate string, entry date/time, image, registration return or rental agreement**. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="6"}

Christensen’s **May 31, 2013 declaration**, **DE 29-4, ¶29**, reproduced in **DE 99-1, p. 88**, recounts what Berberich told him about north-gate records and names additional purported visitors. This is sworn testimony about the source’s account, **not Christensen’s authentication of the underlying entries**. Berberich’s own acquired declaration does not supply the comparison; that omission is not a retraction. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="7"}

Two FBI communications add context but no visible plate evidence:

- **April 3, 2002:** **DE 97-2, pp. 72–74 / BULLDOG-74–76** refers to connections between family members and the **investigation**.
- **April 16, 2002:** *Government Exhibits*, **pp. 35–36 / SARASOTA-5–6**, uses broader language about connections with individuals associated with the attacks.

Neither acquired communication exposes the supposed gate entry, image or Atta/Jarrah vehicle comparison. Their different wording should be preserved rather than combined into a stronger claim. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="8"}

### The negative evidence—and its limits

The strongest acquired counterstatement is the **April 30, 2014 briefing memorandum**, updated **May 6, 2014**, titled **“Al-Hiijjii Family.”** The public copy is **DE 68-1, docket pp. 22–25**, in case **16-cv-61289-CMA**; the linked PDF has four pages.

On **PDF p. 3 / Broward Bulldog-3**, it says the FBI **did not obtain the gate records**. The same page states:

> “There is no actual documentation of searches and work done to rule out connections.”

That is a primary record of the later briefing, not a contemporaneous negative plate-comparison worksheet. [Acquired memorandum](https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/document.pdf#page=3). :chatgpt-content-reference{index="9"}

The official **March 2015 9/11 Review Commission report**, **printed pp. 105–107 / PDF pp. 106–108**, found the allegations unsubstantiated. It reports that the author could not substantiate the April 2002 communication. **Footnotes 356–359 cite the April 30 briefing memorandum**; I did not acquire the author’s underlying interview record. These are significant contrary findings, but they do not provide a reproducible gate comparison. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="10"}

Other acquired negatives concern different tests:

- **FDLE IR 253, p. 2:** negative name checks through the regional task force.
- **FDLE SI-73-1999, IR 1, PDF p. 11:** negative financial/database checks and driver-license queries for Esam and Deborah Ghazzawi.
- **Government Exhibits, pp. 62–64 / SARASOTA-33–35:** a **September 2011** analyst account of negative telephone searches.

None is a negative comparison of an identified gate photograph against a vehicle registration. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="11"}

## 4. Vehicle comparators actually acquired

| Comparator | Document and pinpoint | What it establishes |
|---|---|---|
| **Atta-associated Pontiac: Florida D79DDV** | Official Moussaoui prosecution exhibit **OG00013, p. 26**, “Hijackers’ True Name Usage / 2001”; entry dated **July 7, 2000** | Trial summary identifies a **1989 Pontiac Grand Prix**. I acquired the summary, not the underlying bill-of-sale/title packet. |
| **Al-Shehhi and the same plate: D79DDV** | Official exhibit **MM01011, p. 2**, Florida driver-license application/receipt, **April 12, 2001** | The actual application carries **D79DDV**. A photograph of that plate alone cannot uniquely identify Atta as the driver. |
| **Jarrah-associated Eclipse: Florida T92QBT** | **OG00013, p. 27**, entry dated **November 3, 2000** | Trial summary identifies a **1990 Mitsubishi Eclipse** and a disposal affidavit dated **September 6, 2001**, referencing **M-MMA-00021792–3**. The underlying title and affidavit were not acquired. |
| **UMS-insured van: New Jersey JRJ13Y** | FBI release **1138796-001, 303A-NK-105536, section 2, pp. 78–79** | Registration and insurance scans share **VIN 1GCEG15W4Y1142815**. Registration says **2000 Chevrolet van**, Vault Trust; insurance says **2000 GMC/van**, insured **Urban Moving Systems Inc.**, effective **August 6–October 6, 2001**. The VIN links these two records despite their make descriptions. |

The hijacker comparators come from the court’s official [OG00013](https://coop.vaed.uscourts.gov/moussaoui/exhibits/prosecution/OG00013.pdf) and [MM01011](https://coop.vaed.uscourts.gov/moussaoui/exhibits/prosecution/MM01011.pdf). The UMS documents were acquired from a public mirror of the [FBI section 2 release](https://archive.org/download/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%202.pdf#page=78), not an agency-hosted copy. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="12"}

**Rental distinction:** OG00013, **p. 27**, separately lists Jarrah’s **September 7, 2001 Budget rental**, a Mitsubishi Galant, **New Jersey LJE87L**, referring to exhibit **NK00051**. I acquired that reference, not the rental agreement. It is a different vehicle from the Eclipse; neither has been joined to an acquired Prestancia entry. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="13"}

The **1995 residence Chevrolet** and **2000 UMS van** have incompatible recorded year/body descriptions. Their common Chevrolet description provides no affirmative match. The redacted Sarasota VIN prevents the definitive vehicle-identity comparison.

## 5. UMS, Max and the August 27 moving truck

A **September 21, 2001 Newark FBI communication**, describing a **September 17 visit**, records **Urban Moving Systems Inc.** and **Max Movers Inc.** among names displayed at the Weehawken office: **303A-NK-105536, section 5, p. 1**. This establishes observed co-location, not that every vehicle belonged to both companies.

Its **pp. 2–4** identify additional vehicles, including **NY 99260-JA and 99258-JA** associated with **4 G’s Truck Renting**, and Urban-marked trucks bearing **NJ X-8221M, X87-D66 and X61-C75**. This is a dated snapshot, not a complete fleet history. No acquired Sarasota plate matches any of them. [Acquired FBI section 5](https://archive.org/download/DancingIsraelisFBIReport/fbi%20report%20section%205.pdf#page=1).

The Sarasota moving-truck lead is real **as a reported account**: **FDLE SI-73-1999, IR 1, PDF p. 11** attributes to Kost the statement that a truck moved the family out on **August 27, 2001**. It gives **no company, plate, VIN, driver, destination or job number**. Page 10 labels **The National Rural Development & Finance Corporation** and **Esam Arabian Projects Est.** as *possible businesses*; neither is identified as the mover. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="14"}

An independently acquired UMS record mentions approximately the same date: **Philadelphia FBI report, August 13, 2002, 303C-PH-C91946, serial 33, p. 5** describes an interview account of a UMS worker in **Brooklyn** asking another person to help deliver furniture to **Arkansas** around **August 27, 2001**. That geographical account does not establish a Sarasota job, confirm the Arkansas job’s completion, or exclude other crews. [Acquired report, p. 5](https://www.israellobby.org/UrbanMoving/1169683-001%20---%20303C-PH-C91946-Serial%2033%20---%20Section%201%20%281037754%29.pdf#page=5).

**No authenticated shared person, customer, company transaction, vehicle or moving job connecting these Sarasota records to UMS/Max was located.**

## 6. What would falsify the proposed matches?

| Proposed identification | Decisive test or falsifying evidence |
|---|---|
| **Gate vehicle → Atta’s Pontiac or Jarrah’s Eclipse** | The original image and timestamp, full plate **and state**, then date-specific registration/VIN records. A different plate/state or vehicle assignment defeats that vehicle identification. |
| **Matched vehicle → Atta or Jarrah personally driving** | Contemporaneous driver-ID entry, identifiable image or equivalent evidence. **D79DDV’s appearance on al-Shehhi’s application already defeats an exclusively-Atta inference from the plate alone.** It does not itself disprove an Atta visit. |
| **Community entry → visit to 4224 Escondito** | Original host/address field and related entry records. An entry naming another destination defeats the claim that that entry documents a visit to 4224; it cannot alone exclude an additional visit. |
| **TP2844 residence vehicle → the identified UMS van** | Unredacted VIN/title. A different VIN decisively excludes the particular van **1GCEG15W4Y1142815**, without addressing every UMS vehicle. |
| **August 27 truck → UMS/Max** | Original moving contract, dispatch, payment/bill of lading, or gate image with vehicle identification. A uniquely documented different mover/vehicle defeats that specific identification. |
| **FBI never acquired gate records** | An authenticated FBI receipt, evidence inventory, attachment or retained gate-record copy would contradict the 2014 briefing. A sheriff-only receipt would establish sheriff custody, not necessarily FBI receipt. |

## 7. Unsuccessful searches and remaining gaps

The bounded public search covered the supplied repository, litigation exhibits and later releases, FBI/Vault material including the [Executive Order 14040 release index](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040), and 2021–2026 searches for Sarasota/Prestancia gate records. Searches of six public UMS OCR derivatives and the acquired Philadelphia report for Sarasota, Prestancia, Ghazzawi, al-Hijji, Escondito and the two possible companies produced no connecting record. OCR, redactions and incomplete indexing limit that result; this was not a page-by-page review of the entire EO 14040 corpus. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="15"}

Still unacquired are the **2000–2001 gate entries and images; date-specific gate-to-DMV/rental returns; positive or negative plate-comparison worksheets; gate-media seizure/receipt/transfer records; retention or destruction documentation; and a Sarasota moving-job record**.

The evidentiary gap is therefore specific: **documented vehicle identities exist, and accounts of gate matching exist, but the original records needed to connect them have not been acquired.** Neither that gap nor the conflicting later accounts establishes misconduct.

content.text: Please conduct deep research into the original Prestancia, Sarasota gate logs and license-plate images and any FBI or sheriff plate-to-person comparisons for 2000–2001. Start with https://github.com/AveLyra/911-conspiracy-investigation/blob/main/investigation/broader-evidence/sarasota-gate-fbi-source-chronology-2026-11-11/README.md and the litigation exhibit https://www.floridabulldog.org/wp-content/uploads/2012/09/Government-Exhibits.pdf. Trace custodians, retention, receipt and transfer records; locate original entries, images, registration/rental matches and positive and negative comparisons. Compare any authenticated names, companies, vehicles and dates with UMS and Max without assuming a link. Distinguish the postal TP2844 residence vehicle from visitor-gate vehicles. Investigate the reported Atta/Jarrah match and counterevidence; cite exact pages and source custody and record unsuccessful searches. Do not contact anyone or submit requests. Return what was actually acquired and what would falsify each proposed match.

Page 10 labels **The National Rural Development & Finance Corporation** and **Esam Arabian Projects Est.** as *possible businesses*; neither is identified as the mover. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="14"}

An independently acquired UMS record mentions approximately the same date: **Philadelphia FBI report, August 13, 2002, 303C-PH-C91946, serial 33, p. 5** describes an interview account of a UMS worker in **Brooklyn** asking another person to help deliver furniture to **Arkansas** around **August 27, 2001**. That geographical account does not establish a Sarasota job, confirm the Arkansas job’s completion, or exclude other crews. [Acquired report, p. 5](https://www.israellobby.org/UrbanMoving/1169683-001%20---%20303C-PH-C91946-Serial%2033%20---%20Section%201%20%281037754%29.pdf#page=5).

**No authenticated shared person, customer, company transaction, vehicle or moving job connecting these Sarasota records to UMS/Max was located.**

## 6. What would falsify the proposed matches?

| Proposed identification | Decisive test or falsifying evidence |
|---|---|
| **Gate vehicle → Atta’s Pontiac or Jarrah’s Eclipse** | The original image and timestamp, full plate **and state**, then date-specific registration/VIN records. A different plate/state or vehicle assignment defeats that vehicle identification. |
| **Matched vehicle → Atta or Jarrah personally driving** | Contemporaneous driver-ID entry, identifiable image or equivalent evidence. **D79DDV’s appearance on al-Shehhi’s application already defeats an exclusively-Atta inference from the plate alone.** It does not itself disprove an Atta visit. |
| **Community entry → visit to 4224 Escondito** | Original host/address field and related entry records. An entry naming another destination defeats the claim that that entry documents a visit to 4224; it cannot alone exclude an additional visit. |
| **TP2844 residence vehicle → the identified UMS van** | Unredacted VIN/title. A different VIN decisively excludes the particular van **1GCEG15W4Y1142815**, without addressing every UMS vehicle. |
| **August 27 truck → UMS/Max** | Original moving contract, dispatch, payment/bill of lading, or gate image with vehicle identification. A uniquely documented different mover/vehicle defeats that specific identification. |
| **FBI never acquired gate records** | An authenticated FBI receipt, evidence inventory, attachment or retained gate-record copy would contradict the 2014 briefing. A sheriff-only receipt would establish sheriff custody, not necessarily FBI receipt. |

## 7. Unsuccessful searches and remaining gaps

The bounded public search covered the supplied repository, litigation exhibits and later releases, FBI/Vault material including the [Executive Order 14040 release index](https://vault.fbi.gov/9-11-attacks-investigation-and-related-materials/9-11-material-released-in-response-to-executive-order-14040), and 2021–2026 searches for Sarasota/Prestancia gate records. Searches of six public UMS OCR derivatives and the acquired Philadelphia report for Sarasota, Prestancia, Ghazzawi, al-Hijji, Escondito and the two possible companies produced no connecting record. OCR, redactions and incomplete indexing limit that result; this was not a page-by-page review of the entire EO 14040 corpus. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="15"}

Still unacquired are the **2000–2001 gate entries and images; date-specific gate-to-DMV/rental returns; positive or negative plate-comparison worksheets; gate-media seizure/receipt/transfer records; retention or destruction documentation; and a Sarasota moving-job record**.

The evidentiary gap is therefore specific: **documented vehicle identities exist, and accounts of gate matching exist, but the original records needed to connect them have not been acquired.** Neither that gap nor the conflicting later accounts establishes misconduct.

Distinguish it from later FAA response packets and the separate NORAD response. Use dates, exact titles, archival identifiers and page numbers to establish matches; distinguish a catalog reference from an acquired document. items.text:
**I recovered an official reproduction of the original FAA response and contemporaneous evidence of its receipt, but not a separately corrected 2003 response or its transmittal.** I also recovered an actual OIG case-closure record. That establishes closure of the investigation; it does not establish completion of the recommended FAA correction.

Below, **acquired** means an inspected public scan or official reproduction. **Catalog-only** means the underlying document was not acquired. Page numbers are PDF pages unless identified as printed pages.

## The original 2003 FAA response and receipt

The identifiable response is **“FAA communications with NORAD / On September 11, 2001.”** An official reproduction appears in **Appendix 5, PDF p. 30**, of DOT OIG’s **“ACTION: Results of OIG Investigation of 9/11 Commission Staff Referral,” August 31, 2006, Report No. CC-2006-085**. The report dates submission to the evening of **May 22, 2003**; the reproduced statement itself has no dated transmittal or signature. **Status: acquired official reproduction, not the original transmission record.** :chatgpt-content-reference{index="0"}

There is strong contemporaneous receipt evidence. In the **May 23, 2003 hearing transcript, PDF p. 78**, Richard Ben-Veniste says Jane Garvey communicated with staff the previous evening, identifies the FAA statement by title, and reads it into the record. The matching text asserts immediate participation by the Air Force liaison on a telephone bridge and formal notification concerning American 77 at **9:24 a.m.**, with information conveyed earlier. This establishes receipt of that original statement—not receipt of a later correction. [Original hearing PDF, p. 78](https://www.911commission.gov/archive/hearing2/9-11Commission_Hearing_2003-05-23.pdf#page=78). :chatgpt-content-reference{index="1"}

## Correction and administrative disposition

The **2006 OIG report, pp. 9–10**, says the liaison actually joined after the Pentagon impact and that executives subsequently learned of the error without correcting it with the Commission. **Page 12, recommendations 1–2**, calls for correcting the QFR and considering administrative action regarding two current executives. These are recommendations, not implementation records. **Page 2** reports no evidence supporting knowing false statements, purposeful omission, or intentional failure to correct. That finding must remain distinct from the documented inaccuracy and failure to act. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="2"}

Two additional acquired records establish narrower administrative outcomes:

| Record | Exact locator | What it establishes |
|---|---|---|
| **September 27, 2004**, Kenneth Mead to Marion Blakey, **“ACTION: Inaccurate Posting on FAA Website, Re: 9/11/01 Chronology”** | DOT OIG release **FI-2012-0005**, PDF **p. 168** | Reports revision of an FAA website fact sheet. This concerns the website chronology. |
| **“TIGR CASE INPUT SHEET”**, investigation **042R0122001** | Same release, PDF **p. 6** | Records **Close Investigation Date: December 12, 2006**. The same-date **“Investigation Quarterly Synopsis,”** PDF **pp. 13, 15–16**, corroborates the final case update. |

Source: [public copy of DOT OIG’s agency release, hosted by GovernmentAttic](https://www.governmentattic.org/6docs/DOT-OIG-FAA9-11_2001-2006.pdf).

**Inference:** These records establish a website correction and closure of the OIG investigation. Neither demonstrates that FAA filed a corrected Commission QFR or completed personnel action.

**Unresolved dating conflict:** The synopsis, PDF **p. 13 / internal p. 1**, describes a **July 24, 2004** referral; the published OIG report, **p. 1**, identifies a referral letter dated **July 29, 2004**. I did not acquire the original letter to resolve that difference. [Synopsis](https://www.governmentattic.org/6docs/DOT-OIG-FAA9-11_2001-2006.pdf#page=13). :chatgpt-content-reference{index="3"}

## Later FAA packets: acquired and distinguishable

These records belong to **RG 237, series NAID 7419198**. Their internal dates and subjects distinguish them from the May 2003 answer. The AWA numbers, boxes and NAIDs are corroborated by NARA’s finding aids; the conclusions below also use the acquired PDFs. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}

| Acquired record and archival identifier | Date and pages | Identification |
|---|---|---|
| **“FAA QUESTIONS FOR THE RECORD No.1”** — **AWA-336**, box **94**, **NAID 7601901** | **May 25, 2004**, dated on **p. 3**; three pages | Daniel Marcus’s questions concerning airspace closure, reopening and specified departure flights. Responses requested by June 8. [Original PDF](https://catalog.archives.gov/medialz/dc-metro/rg-237/7419198-9-11-faa/5-Miscellaneous/e-Other/5-AWA-336-Record-FAA-Questions-for-the-Record-No-1.pdf). |
| Catalog wording **“Letter Responses to Questions for the Record No 1”** — **AWA-335**, box **94**, **NAID 7601900**; also **AWA-819**, box **97**, **NAID 34913651** | **June 8, 2004**, cover letter **p. 1** in each; **20** and **19** pages respectively | Shirley Miller to Daniel Marcus, expressly answering the **May 25, 2004** request. These are separately cataloged, overlapping packets; I do not characterize them as identical copies. [AWA-335 PDF](https://catalog.archives.gov/medialz/dc-metro/rg-237/7419198-9-11-faa/5-Miscellaneous/e-Other/5-AWA-335-Letter-Responses-to-Questions-for-the-Record-No-1.pdf); [AWA-819 PDF](https://catalog.archives.gov/medialz/dc-metro/rg-237/7419198-9-11-faa/5-e-other/5-AWA-819-Letter-Responses-to-Questions-for-the-Record-No-1-REDACT-SEALED.pdf). |
| Catalog wording **“Emails FAA Questions for the Record No 1”** — **AWA-338**, box **94**, **NAID 34913207** | **June 10 and June 16, 2004**, **p. 1**; six-page file | Tom Eldridge thanks Miller for the answers and requests follow-up information; Miller subsequently sends additional answers. This is receipt/follow-up evidence for the **2004** packet. [Original PDF](https://catalog.archives.gov/medialz/dc-metro/rg-237/7419198-9-11-faa/5-e-other/5-AWA-338-Emails-FAA-Questions-for-the-Record-No-1-REDACT-SEALED.pdf). |
| Catalog wording **“Letter DOT Confirmation that DOT-FAA Satisfied Commissions Doc Requests”** — **AWA-823**, box **97**, **NAID 34913657** | **July 8, 2004**, **p. 1**; fax header **July 12, 2004** | Norman Mineta to Kean and Hamilton, certifying completion of reasonable searches and production for **four document requests**. It does not certify correction of the May 2003 QFR. [Original PDF](https://catalog.archives.gov/medialz/dc-metro/rg-237/7419198-9-11-faa/5-e-other/5-AWA-823-Letter-DOT-Confirmation-that-DOT-FAA-Satisfied-Commissions-Doc-Requests-REDACT-SEALED.pdf). |

Two potentially misleading **2003** matches also failed the substantive match:

- **AWA-333, NAID 34913203**, cataloged **“Supplemental to July 5 Response”**: its **p. 1** identifies **DOT Document Request No. Two, July 2, 2003**, and discusses controller information and transcripts. It is not an identified correction to the May 22 QFR. [Original PDF](https://catalog.archives.gov/medialz/dc-metro/rg-237/7419198-9-11-faa/5-e-other/5-AWA-333-Supplemental-to-July-5-Response-REDACT-SEALED.pdf).
- **AWA-673, NAID 7601973**, **“INFORMATION: Presidential 9/11 Commission Final Follow-up Response,” November 7, 2003**, **p. 1**: concerns completion of employee-interview follow-up. Its “Final Follow-up” title does not identify the sought correction. [Original PDF](https://catalog.archives.gov/medialz/dc-metro/rg-237/7419198-9-11-faa/5-Miscellaneous/e-Other/5-AWA-673-Memo-Presidential-9-11-Commission-Final-Follow-up-Response.pdf).

## Separate NORAD response and contradictory evidence

The supplied **“NORAD QUESTIONS FOR THE RECORD,” ISCAP appeal 2012-047, document 5**, is an acquired **two-page NORAD response**. NARA assigns document date **May 23, 2003** and lists **September 29, 2014** as the appeal release date. Within the document, however, May 23 identifies the **hearing date**; neither page supplies a distinct transmittal or receipt date. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="5"}

On **p. 1, Answer 2**, NORAD says it had no information about American 77 before **9:24**. That conflicts with the FAA statement’s claim of earlier information conveyed through telephone bridges. **Page 2** lists attachments that are absent from this two-page release. It therefore cannot supply the FAA correction or its delivery record. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="6"}

The Commission’s final report provides a further contradiction: **printed p. 34 / PDF p. 51** identifies the **9:24** scramble as responding to the erroneous report that American 11 remained airborne, and places notification that American 77 was **missing** at **9:34**. This establishes the Commission’s revised published account, not an FAA correction’s transmittal. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="7"}

## Catalog-only leads and remaining gaps

The following are **unpaginated NARA catalog descriptions**. I acquired their metadata, not their folder contents:

| Exact catalog title | Archival locator |
|---|---|
| **“FAA”** | RG 148, **Subject Files of Daniel Marcus**, series **2538480**, box **3**, [NAID 2604775](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/2604775) |
| **“5/22-23/2003 Public Hearing”** | Same series, box **6**, [NAID 2604839](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/2604839) |
| **“Referral [NORAD/FAA Misstatements]”** | Same series, box **6**, [NAID 2604844](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/2604844) |
| **“Department of Transportation”** | RG 148, **Subject Files of Steven Dunne**, series **2524846**, box **5**, [NAID 2604691](https://catalog.archives.gov/id/2604691) |

**Unsuccessful searches:** Exact-title and variant searches for a corrected/revised FAA response, QFRs, liaison/bridge corrections and subsequent disposition—in agency releases, Commission records, NARA descriptions and released PDFs—did not authenticate the separate correction. This was a bounded public-record search, not an examination of all paper holdings.

The **December 22, 2011** release letter, **PDF pp. 2–3**, identifies **4,845 responsive pages**, produces **426**, and refers **255 FAA-origin** and **2,241 Commission-origin** pages for separate review. Its closure language concerns the **FOIA request**. [Agency release letter](https://www.governmentattic.org/6docs/DOT-OIG-FAA9-11_2001-2006.pdf#page=2).

**Still missing:** an authenticated corrected 2003 FAA response; its transmission or receipt record; the original referral letter; and a management or personnel record documenting implementation of the OIG recommendations. Those gaps do not establish that a correction was suppressed, ignored, or never existed.
